svg.aria-label: Bars comparing one-way time London to New York: straight fibre about 28 ms, lasers in space about 23 ms
svg.text: London to New York: 5,570 km along the ground. One way, at best:
a perfectly straight fibre, through the sea
5,570 km at two-thirds of the speed of light: 27.9 ms
lasers in space, 550 km up, plus the trips up and down
7,151 km at the speed of light: 23.9 ms
Light in glass travels at about 200,000 km/s (Chapter 17); in a vacuum, 300,000. Over long enough distances, the longer
path through space wins. Real cables aren’t straight, which makes the gap bigger still.

figure.figcaption: Why some people want to send long-distance traffic through space, even when there’s a cable.
